questions: During the episodes, do you lose awareness or become unable to respond?
Are the episodes highly similar to one another each time?
Do you have a period of confusion or marked sleepiness afterward?
Do the episodes begin with a sudden forced turning of your head or eyes to one side?
Does your trunk consistently turn to the same side during the episodes?
Do the movements involve stiffening followed by rhythmic jerking of the limbs?
Have you bitten the side of your tongue during an episode?
Have you lost bladder or bowel control during an episode?
Have you sustained an injury during an episode?
Do you retain any memory of what happens during the episode?
Can someone interrupt the movements or bring you to responsiveness during an episode?
Do the episodes last longer than five minutes?
Do multiple episodes occur without you returning to your usual level of awareness between them?
Have you ever had similar episodes before?
Have you previously been diagnosed with epilepsy or another seizure disorder?
Are you currently taking an antiseizure medication?
Have you recently missed doses or stopped an antiseizure medication?
Did the episodes begin after a recent head injury, stroke, brain infection, or brain surgery?
Have you recently had a fever or serious infection?
Do you use alcohol or recreational drugs, or have you recently stopped using them?
Were the episodes preceded by lightheadedness, sweating, nausea, or visual dimming?
Do the episodes occur only in particular situations or in the presence of specific emotional stress?
Have you ever had panic attacks or episodes of dissociation?
Is there a possibility that you are pregnant?

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Genetic (idiopathic) generalized epilepsy causing generalized tonic-clonic seizures with ictal axial/trunk turning

Alternative 1: Focal epilepsy with rapid secondary bilateral synchrony, producing versive seizures

Alternative 2: Structural frontal-lobe epilepsy with bilateral propagation

Alternative 3: Psychogenic nonepileptic seizures occurring coincidentally with generalized epileptiform discharges
